reading_plan: Source title: Ohio Revised Code Sections 3313.6028 (Literacy curriculum), 3313.608 (Third-grade reading guarantee), and 3319.2310 (Science of reading training for licensed educators). Source type: government_policy. The first look shows a 19-page compilation of three enacted, codified Ohio statutes, not a pending bill or guidance document: 3313.6028 (A)-(F), effective October 9, 2026; 3313.608 (A)-(K), effective September 30, 2025; and 3319.2310 (A)-(D), effective October 9, 2026. The first section includes an LSC composite-amendment note; all three have available-version lists. The provisions are densely nested, especially the guarantee's exceptions and teacher qualifications, though the pages are generously spaced. I will proceed in printed order, usually by subsection and no more than about a page per substantive step, splitting long lists while preserving their governing conditions. I will distinguish operative text from editorial metadata and retain historical dates as printed. The supplied page images show clean code text with blue underlined cross-reference links, not amendment strikeouts or insertion markup. Claims use paraphrase unless exact wording is confidently reproduced. Support records stated purposes or incorporated legal criteria and cross-references, not invented empirical evidence; an empty support array means no separate basis is given. External citations are transcribed as printed, with line-wrap whitespace normalized and no completed bibliographic entries.

reading_path.moves: Defines science of reading across Title XXXIII and three-cueing for this section. The definition takes an affirmative instructional position and expressly excludes a family of models.

claims.text: For Title XXXIII of the Revised Code, science of reading means an interdisciplinary body of scientific evidence with all four listed characteristics.
Under (A)(1)(a), that evidence informs how students learn to read and write proficiently.
Under (A)(1)(b), that evidence explains why some students have difficulty with reading and writing.

Under (A)(1)(c), that evidence indicates that all students benefit from explicit and systematic instruction in phonemic awareness, phonics, vocabulary, fluency, comprehension, and writing to become effective readers.
Under (A)(1)(d), that evidence does not rely on any model of teaching students to read based on meaning, structure and syntax, and visual cues, including a three-cueing approach.
For this section, three-cueing approach means any model of teaching students to read based on meaning, structure and syntax, and visual cues.

reading_path.meaning: Before assigning duties, the section sets both the scope of its preferred evidence and the instructional approach it excludes. It names no particular research study for these definitional statements.

reading_path.moves: Assigns list-making, evaluation, publication, and disclosure duties to the department of education and workforce.

claims.text: The department shall establish a list of high-quality English language arts core curriculum and instructional materials and a list of evidence-based reading intervention programs, aligned with the science of reading and strategies for effective literacy instruction.

The department shall establish a rubric and scoring system evaluating whether or to what extent English language arts core curricula facilitate a student's skill building and sequential advancement through mastery.
The department shall post the rubric and scoring system on its publicly accessible website.
Upon request, the department shall provide a scored rubric to the entity that submitted a curriculum for scoring and to any Ohio general assembly member.

reading_path.meaning: The definition now becomes an administrative selection and evaluation framework; public access to the scoring method is broader than the expressly specified access to scored rubrics.

claims.text: Every individual employed by a district or other public school as a teacher, administrator, school psychologist, or speech-language pathologist shall complete science-of-reading training in accordance with (C).
Teachers and administrators hired before July 1, 2025, shall complete the (B)(2) course or a (B)(3) listed course by June 30, 2030, and every five years thereafter.

reading_path.meaning: A broad duty is implemented through separate schedules. The first schedule requires the reinforcement course or an approved more rigorous course, without adding an introductory-course duty in (C)(1).

reading_path.moves: Sets the newer-hire schedule, exempts verified recent preparation from the introduction, and assigns verification and similarity determinations.

claims.text: Teachers and administrators hired on or after July 1, 2025, shall complete the (B)(1) introduction within one year of hire.
They shall complete the (B)(2) course or a (B)(3) listed course every five years thereafter.

The introduction shall not be required if the district superintendent or other public school head administrator verifies that within five years before hire the individual completed that training or similar training as determined by the department.

The introduction also shall not be required upon that verification of appropriate science-of-reading coursework completed within five years before hire as part of an educator or licensure preparation program.

reading_path.meaning: Recent qualifying preparation removes the introductory requirement, while the text leaves the recurring-course requirement in place. The exception is tied to verification and a five-year lookback.

reading_path.moves: Sets a role-specific schedule for school psychologists and speech-language pathologists, without a hire-date split.

claims.text: School psychologists and speech-language pathologists employed by districts or other public schools shall complete the (B)(1) introduction by June 30, 2027.
They shall complete the (B)(2) course or a (B)(3) listed course every five years thereafter.

reading_path.meaning: The same course structure applies to these specialists, but their initial deadline is fixed rather than calculated from hiring.

reading_path.moves: Requires licensure credit and carryover for division (B) training. This echoes 3313.6028(E) but applies to these courses and individuals. The ending lists enactment and amendment history.

claims.text: A professional development committee established under section 3319.22 shall count division (B) training toward educator licensure-renewal professional development requirements.

support.text: This provision incorporates or cross-references the following law; the document does not reproduce the external provisions in full.

claims.text: The committee shall permit an individual to apply hours earned above the minimum renewal-coursework requirement to the next renewal period for that license.
The available-version list records enactment on September 30, 2025, by House Bill 96 and amendment on October 9, 2026, by House Bill 455, both in the 136th General Assembly.
